questions.q: Why does an incremental extract filtered only on SystemModstamp fail to catch deleted records?
options: A deleted row no longer exists to be returned by any query, so a query looking for recently-changed rows simply never sees it
SystemModstamp is updated to a special value when a record is deleted
Deleted records are automatically re-inserted by Salesforce after 24 hours
SystemModstamp only applies to custom objects, not standard objects
questions.explain: A query filtering on SystemModstamp can only return rows that still exist -- a deleted record is gone, not merely changed, so it never appears in the result set at all.

questions.q: What does Change Data Capture (CDC) publish that a plain incremental SystemModstamp extract does not?
options: CDC publishes only create events, same as an incremental extract
CDC explicitly publishes delete and undelete events as part of its event stream, in addition to creates and updates
CDC can only be used on custom objects, never standard objects
CDC replaces the need for any object permissions
questions.explain: CDC's event stream includes delete and undelete operations explicitly, which is exactly what closes the gap a SystemModstamp-only incremental extract leaves open.

questions.q: Why does Doverfield route its high-volume Salesforce data extraction through the Bulk API rather than the standard REST API?
options: The Bulk API is designed for large-volume asynchronous operations, isolating heavy extraction load from the API capacity used by day-to-day transactional and UI traffic
The standard REST API cannot return more than ten records total
The Bulk API does not count against any Salesforce API limits
Bulk API and REST API return data in incompatible formats that cannot both be used in the same org
questions.explain: Treating a large extract as a sequence of small synchronous REST calls would compete with the org's regular traffic for the same request capacity -- the Bulk API exists specifically to move large data sets efficiently instead.

questions.q: What is a 'watermark' in the context of an incremental extract job?
options: A visual marking added to exported files to prevent copying
The timestamp or marker the job uses to know where the previous successful run left off, so the next run only pulls what changed since then
A Salesforce field that marks a record as read-only
The maximum number of rows a single Bulk API job can return
questions.explain: The watermark is what makes an incremental extract 'incremental' at all -- without a correctly tracked and recovered watermark, the job can't reliably know what's new since last time.

questions.q: In Doverfield's actual design, which objects use CDC versus a scheduled incremental Bulk API pull?
options: All objects use CDC exclusively, with no scheduled pulls at all

Objects where deletes matter and real-time freshness is worth the complexity (like Opportunity and Account) use CDC, while most other objects use a scheduled incremental pull with periodic full reconciliation for deletes
All objects use scheduled full extracts only, since CDC was ruled out entirely
CDC is used only for objects that have no delete events at all
questions.explain: Doverfield makes a deliberate, selective trade-off: CDC where real-time freshness and reliable deletes justify the added complexity, and a simpler scheduled incremental pull plus periodic reconciliation everywhere else.
